newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK - U.S. 10-year note auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK - U.S. 10-year note auction.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury's 10-year note auction will be the focus of the market's attention on Tuesday and analysts said the sale could get a slightly tentative reception.

"I would not expect a banner reception only because I think the market has priced in a lot of good news right now," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
"There's not much room for yields to go lower unless you get further confirmation of a slowdown in the economy."
The market is getting some significant economic data on Friday and next week, analysts said.
On Friday, the government will release the September Producer Price Index (PPI) and retail sales data. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September is due next week.
"You get important data on Friday and you have to bid for the 10-years ahead of those data," said Flanagan. "That could play a restraining role."
That there are no first-tier economic data due on Tuesday will only make the auction stand out more as the day's most prominent feature.

The market gets the BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales report at 0900 EDT. In the week ended September 28, it fell 1.2 percent. The Lynch Jones & Ryan Redbook store sale sales report is due at 1455 EDT/1855 GMT. It slipped 0.4 percent in the week ended September 28.

"There's no data to speak of except the normal Tuesday roster of weekly store sales reports," said Richard Koss, economist at Maria Fiorini Ramirez Inc. "We've gotten used to seeing soft weekly numbers so there's a touch of vulnerability here if the numbers come out on the stronger side."
The September Richmond Federal Reserve survey, due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, should also have minimal impact, Koss said.

The Treasury last sold 10-year notes in its quarterly refunding on August 7. The bid was weak, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.22 to one, compared with the previous 10-year Treasury note auction -- one that was not part of a quarterly refunding effort -- when the bid-cover ratio was 2.66 to one, said Flanagn.
Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A., said the auction takes placeas the market is still putting September's employment report, released Friday, into perspective.

"We're very close to the high end of the six-month trding range as we approach the 10-year auction," Stiles observed. "The underlying sentiment is positive, but there's some concern about the very next trade -- depending on how the next inflation numbers play out."
One positive factor for the auction was that profit-taking on Monday pushed the 10-year note yield to 6.52 percent in when-issued trade from below 6.50 percent at the close on Friday.
"That makes the auction less threatening," said Stiles, "but it still looks like a challenge." -- 212-859-1679
